report.root_cause: The order-gateway 2.4.0 deploy (CHG-4310, connection pooling changes, still active) drove order-gateway-2 into JVM heap exhaustion, with heap at 90-100% and GC pauses up to 833 ms, which pushed gateway latency to about 437-593 ms while order-gateway-1 stayed at about 5 ms. reference-db was healthy and no MRX maintenance window was found, so the database is not the cause.
report.summary: I restarted only order-gateway-2 under INC-5203 and its latency dropped to 5 ms with error rate 0.001 and memory at 55.6%. The reviewer found memory climbing again on the same version (55.3% at 11:22, 57.4% at 11:29, while order-gateway-1 stays flat at 55.0%), so the incident is not confirmed resolved; CHG-4310 is still active and needs an owner decision on rollback, and ALR-1001 was not verified cleared.

report.summary: order-gateway-2 was restarted alone at 11:17 (ACT-001), and latency dropped back to 5.0ms with no new GC warnings. The reviewer reports INC-5203 as not over: order-gateway-2 memory is climbing again (55.0% to 56.2% in about three minutes), and CHG-4310 is still active, so the exhaustion will likely return. I did not roll back CHG-4310 because the request was limited to restarting order-gateway-2; a rollback or fix of CHG-4310 needs a separate decision, and order-gateway-2 memory needs continued monitoring. Network and database reported no maintenance windows, but their checks were not complete, so restart constraints were not fully verified.

report.summary: INC-1 / ALR-1001 is not resolved: the reviewer confirmed order-gateway aggregate latency is still about 185 ms against a threshold below 20 ms, and the order-gateway to reference-db link is still degraded. Nothing was routed to site B, CHG-4310 was not touched, and the per-instance (5 ms) versus aggregate (185 ms) latency mismatch remains unexplained.

report.root_cause: Likely memory leak or heap exhaustion in order-gateway-2 (order-gateway 2.4.0, change CHG-4310 connection pooling still active). Heap climbed to 95-100% with GC pauses of 84-881 ms, ending in an OutOfMemoryError and process exit at 10:27. This is not confirmed as the source of ALR-1001, and CHG-4310 causation is not verified. reference-db was ruled out as the cause (healthy, no MRX window).
report.summary: order-gateway-2 ran out of heap and exited at 10:27, which pushed aggregate error rate to about 10% and drove the alert storm for INC-9101. It came back ready at 10:29, and the reviewer confirmed latency 5 ms and error rate 0.1% at 10:33, with order-gateway-2 heap at about 56% and rising. Caveats: no remediation changed the cause, CHG-4310 rollback safety and open-session impact were never verified, the ALR-1001 origin is unconfirmed, and memory could climb again, so the recurrence should be watched and CHG-4310 decided by a human.

This is supported by timing and by the rollback, but it is not proven. The database (reference-db) and the order-gateway to matching-engine link were checked and found healthy, so they are not the cause.
report.summary: Remediation rolled back CHG-4310 to version 2.3.9 (ACT-001, completed 10:23) and isolated order-gateway-2 from rotation (ACT-002, completed 10:29), but the reviewer has not confirmed recovery. order-gateway-1 was last seen at 55% memory and 7.5 ms latency, yet it is now carrying the full load alone with queue depth rising from 0 to 25, and the follow-up verification failed because the tool budget ran out. No MRX maintenance window could be verified because exchange_status returned no data, and order-gateway-2 is not restarted pending team approval, so the incident needs a fresh verification and human decision.
